Minneapolis-St. Paul is 'Medical Alley', the densest medical-device cluster in the US: Medtronic (operational HQ, Fridley/Mounds View), Boston Scientific (Arden Hills, Maple Grove), Abbott (former St. Jude Medical, St. Paul), plus hundreds of device startups, contract manufacturers, regulatory consultancies and specialist investors; Medical Alley counts ~1,000 health startups and 200+ investor members, and an estimated 80-90% of US implantable devices are engineered or made in the state. Eden Prairie itself hosts Starkey Hearing Technologies (largest US hearing-aid maker, consumer device) and UnitedHealth/Optum operations; Mayo Clinic (Rochester) and the University of Minnesota (Medical Devices Center, Earl Bakken Center) supply clinical and engineering partners. Minnesota has 32,550 device jobs at 3.97x the national concentration and $5.9B of bioscience VC in 2021-25 (40% of it device).

Dobermans appear on many carriers' restricted/'aggressive breed' lists (commonly alongside pit bulls, Rottweilers, chows, Akitas, wolf hybrids); carriers reported to use such lists include Allstate, Farmers (Farmers often restricts only pit bulls/Rottweilers/wolf hybrids), Liberty Mutual, Travelers and Lemonade, though sources conflict on Allstate and Liberty Mutual. State Farm does not ask breed, only bite history (but writes no new homeowners policies in CA, MA, RI); USAA (military-eligible only), Chubb, Amica and Nationwide are reported to underwrite on bite history rather than breed. A separate canine-liability or umbrella policy is the fallback where a carrier excludes the breed. Lists vary by state and change; confirm at quote time.

Bust: Brightline West has not started heavy construction due to funding delays (Oct 2026); two Henderson hyperscale data-center projects collapsed in 2026 (Trammell Crow's, and a $1.5-2B plan on BLM land). Visitors fell 7.5% in 2025 and the metro lost 4,700 jobs Sep-Nov 2025.

IN: Pivot Bio moved its HQ from Berkeley to Minnetonka (Mar 2026); Graco is moving from Minneapolis to suburban Dayton by mid-2027 (within metro). Spin-offs: 3M spun off Solventum (2024) and Medtronic IPO'd MiniMed ($560M, Mar 2026) and split it off (Oct 2026). Bust: UnitedHealth (Minnetonka; Optum in Eden Prairie) saw its CEO resign amid a DOJ Medicare probe (May 2025) and lost ~$300B in market value; Optum closed 16 clinics (Nov 2025). Target cut 1,800 corporate jobs (Oct 2025), and Eden Prairie-based C.H. Robinson's headcount is down 31% since 2022 under its AI push.

IN: Walmart told most remote staff and most workers in its Dallas, Atlanta and Toronto offices to relocate, mostly to Bentonville (May 2024), while cutting several hundred campus roles. Tyson closed its Chicago, Downers Grove and Dakota Dunes corporate offices and moved ~1,000 staff to its Springdale HQ (announced Oct 2022). Investment: Walmart opened its 350-acre Home Office campus on Jan 17, 2025; the 12th and last office building opened in Jan 2026, with ~15,000 HQ staff. OUT: Walmart's 2025 consolidation also sent some roles to Sunnyvale, Bellevue and Hoboken. There were no major busts.

PG&E owns the distribution grid for nearly all homes; CleanPowerSF (SFPUC community choice program) supplies the generation and SFPUC Hetch Hetchy Power serves city facilities and some new developments. No wage income tax, but a 7% capital-gains excise (9.9% on gains over $1M from 2025, SB 5813) applies above a ~$278k standard deduction; WA starts from federal net long-term gain, so federally excluded QSBS gain is not taxed (DOR FAQ). SB 6229/HB 2292 to add QSBS back died in the 2026 session. A new 9.9% income tax (ESSB 6346) is scheduled from 2028 without a QSBS add-back. Camas: as WA residents neither spouse owes Oregon tax on wages earned working from home in WA (Oregon taxes non-residents only on Oregon-source income), and a WA resident's stock gain is not Oregon-source, so Oregon's 2026 QSBS add-back does not apply; Marcel works remotely for Red Hat from home in WA, so Oregon tax does not apply to him. Days worked physically in Oregon (e.g. a Portland office) would create Oregon wage tax. Federal: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) raises the per-issuer cap to $15M (10x basis), gross-asset test to $75M and adds 50%/75%/100% exclusion at 3/4/5 years for stock issued after 2025-07-04.

Pennsylvania computes taxable gains under its own personal income tax rules with no IRC conformity (72 P.S. 7303), so the federal §1202 exclusion is fully added back and the gain is taxed at the 3.07% flat rate (about $307,000 on a $10M federally excluded gain, the lowest cost among full-addback states); the 2025 OBBBA expansion is likewise irrelevant for PA purposes. Local earned income tax does not apply to capital gains. Federal: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) raises the per-issuer cap to $15M (10x basis), gross-asset test to $75M and adds 50%/75%/100% exclusion at 3/4/5 years for stock issued after 2025-07-04.

Dobermans appear on many carriers' restricted/'aggressive breed' lists (commonly alongside pit bulls, Rottweilers, chows, Akitas, wolf hybrids); carriers reported to use such lists include Allstate, Farmers (Farmers often restricts only pit bulls/Rottweilers/wolf hybrids), Liberty Mutual, Travelers and Lemonade, though sources conflict on Allstate and Liberty Mutual. State Farm does not ask breed, only bite history (but writes no new homeowners policies in CA, MA, RI); USAA (military-eligible only), Chubb, Amica and Nationwide are reported to underwrite on bite history rather than breed. A separate canine-liability or umbrella policy is the fallback where a carrier excludes the breed. Lists vary by state and change; confirm at quote time.

IN: Burlington Stores is moving its HQ from New Jersey to Schuylkill Yards in University City (Sep 2026, $370M, 2,000 jobs averaging ~$125K). It will be the city's first new Fortune 500 HQ in decades. Hanwha bought Philly Shipyard and pledged $5B for two new docks, aiming to go from under 2 to up to 20 ships a year (Aug 2025). Chubb opened a ~$380M Philadelphia office in 2025. Bust: Comcast is cutting 634 jobs at its Center City HQ as it shifts to AI (Oct 2026), and Amazon closed all six Philly-area Amazon Fresh stores (983 jobs, Jan 2026). The metro lost 3,906 federal jobs (-16.7%) from Jan 2025 to Feb 2026, led by the IRS at 30th & Market. In Chester County, West Chester-based QVC Group went through Chapter 11 (Apr-Aug 2026) after cutting ~900 jobs in 2025.
PA DCED - Burlington Stores to relocate HQ to Philadelphia, 2,000 jobs

IN: The Jul 2025 Pittsburgh Energy and Innovation Summit drew $90B+ in AI, data centre and power pledges. These include the $10B, 4.4 GW gas-fired Homer City data centre campus (power from 2027) and Aligned's $10B, 2 GW campus at the old Bruce Mansfield plant in Shippingport. Nippon Steel, which bought US Steel in Jun 2025 with an $11B pledge, approved a ~$3B hot strip mill at Edgar Thomson in Braddock (Oct 2026, output from 2029). Cranberry-based Westinghouse got an $80B US government deal for new AP1000 reactors (Oct 2025) and $17.5B in DOE loans (Jun 2026). Bust: UPMC cut ~200 jobs and 300 open positions (Jun 2026), after ~1,100 cuts in 2024. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette closed in 2026 (171 jobs).
Sen. McCormick - Fact sheet: more than $90B announced at Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit

IN: Anduril will build Arsenal-2, a $3.7B submarine shipyard at Tradepoint Atlantic in Sparrows Point with 3,100+ permanent jobs (Oct 2026). The state calls it Maryland's largest private investment in over a decade. In Howard County, Saval Foods broke ground on a new HQ and distribution centre in Columbia (Sep 2026). Bust: Federal cuts hit hard. Woodlawn-based Social Security (~10,000 Maryland staff) planned to cut 7,000 jobs nationally (Feb 2025), and HHS laid off 140 in Woodlawn. CMS now has ~1,000 fewer staff than in 2024, and Maryland lost 29,200 federal jobs from Jan 2025 to Apr 2026. IN: Google is building three data centre campuses in Chesterfield County as the anchor of a $9B Virginia investment (2025-26). QTS plans 17 more buildings on 1,100 acres at White Oak in Henrico. Virginia lost 23,500 federal jobs in 2025.

IN: East Hartford-based Pratt & Whitney (~11,000 CT staff) won $4.7B of F135 engine contracts in 2026 for work in East Hartford and Middletown. IN: The Bills' $2.1B Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park opened in 2026 ($850M public money). It is the biggest construction project in Western New York history and keeps the team for 30 years. Moog opened a $150M advanced manufacturing plant at its East Aurora/Elma HQ campus (Aug 2026, 4,300 WNY staff). In Niagara County, TeraWulf's Lake Mariner campus leased ~360 MW of AI capacity to Fluidstack, with Google backing $3.2B (Aug 2025). Smaller wins include Niagara Power Transformer's $71M expansion in Cheektowaga (73 jobs, Oct 2026) and Solstice's $49M R&D expansion in Buffalo. Note: Micron's megafab is near Syracuse, not Buffalo. Bust: Sumitomo closed its Tonawanda tyre plant (~1,500 jobs; announced Nov 2024, shut Feb 2025). M&T made undisclosed layoffs (Sep 2026), and Univera is leaving its Amherst office.
NY Governor - Completion of new $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium

Wisconsin conforms to the IRC as of 2022-12-31, so the older Section 1202 exclusion (up to 100% for stock held 5 years) applies but the 2025 OBBBA expansion (higher cap, 3/4-year tiers) does not (Startup Law Blog); CT Acquisitions lists Wisconsin as following the federal exclusion (survey). Odyssey: How much funding will LA GATOR provide (2026-27 amounts)

Realistically $0 for 2026-27. LA GATOR ESA 2026-27 award levels: $5,243 (55% of MFP) for a non-priority student, $7,626 at or below 250% FPL, $15,253 with an IDEA disability. Entering kindergarten is an eligibility category with no income cap, so a $260k family is eligible on paper for $5,243. But the legislature held funding flat at about $44M (the governor asked for about $88M). That covers about 5,700 students, almost all continuing participants, out of about 17,400 eligible applicants. Funding order: continuing students, then families at or below 250% FPL and students with disabilities, then siblings, then everyone else by application time. A new high-income kindergartner is almost certainly waitlisted; the application window was 1-16 Mar 2026. Separately, Louisiana's nonpublic school tuition deduction (up to $5,000 per child) would be worth about $150 at the 3% flat rate; this could not be re-verified (search budget ran out), so it is not counted. Universal eligibility is planned for 2027-28, subject to appropriations.

Kentucky levies a flat 5% corporate income tax plus the Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET) on corporations, LLCs and LPs: $175 minimum, and entities with Kentucky gross receipts or gross profits of $3M or less pay only the $175; above that the lesser of 0.095% of gross receipts or 0.75% of gross profits (phased in $3M-$6M). Pass-through members get a credit for LLET paid. Louisville Metro also charges a 2.2% occupational licence tax on business net profits (in addition to the payroll tax).

Wilmington is a contract-research (CRO) town: PPD was founded here and is now Thermo Fisher's clinical research business (~1,800 local staff at the 2021 acquisition), spawning a cluster with Alcami, Fortrea, IQVIA, Syneos and others, useful for running clinical studies; Novant Health New Hanover Regional and UNCW (Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, now leaning to blue/climate tech) round it out, with NCBiotech's Southeastern office. Device startups and investors are few; the Triangle (~2 h) holds NC's capital ($1.43B bioscience VC in 2025; device VC $1.1B over 2021-25, device employment 8,471, LQ 0.62).
